profile.reading:
KOMO Plaza West is one of two adjacent structures that make up the KOMO Plaza broadcast complex in the Lower Queen Anne neighborhood of Seattle, a short distance from the Space Needle, alongside its counterpart KOMO Plaza East roughly 30 to 40 meters away. The complex is better known by its former name, Fisher Plaza, after the Fisher family who founded KOMO radio in 1926 and launched KOMO-TV in 1953. Fisher Communications, the family company, owned and operated the site for decades until Sinclair Broadcast Group bought the company in 2013 for about 373.3 million dollars, bringing its Seattle television and radio operations, and this plaza, under Sinclair's ownership.

As with its eastern counterpart, the West structure is presumed to house some combination of studio space, newsroom operations, and the technical plant that supports live broadcasting: transmission and master control equipment, server and storage infrastructure for news and production workflows, and network connectivity linking the site to Sinclair's other properties and to cable, satellite, and streaming distribution. Facilities built for continuous, around the clock broadcast operations of this kind typically require the same category of resilient power, cooling, and redundant infrastructure associated with data centers, even though the business built on top of that infrastructure is television and radio rather than colocation.

The plaza's public record includes a serious electrical fire on July 2, 2009, and a nearby television news helicopter crash in March 2014, both notable enough to appear in later accounts of the site's history. Following Sinclair's September 2021 purchase of several Seattle radio stations operating under the Lotus brand, those stations remained headquartered at KOMO Plaza rather than moving to a separate facility, another indication that the complex continues to function as a working hub rather than a legacy building kept only for its call letters.

No source located during this research distinguishes West from East by street address or by any technical detail specific to one structure over the other, and Sinclair, as a broadcaster, has not published facility-level specifications for either building. The two structures are best understood together, as twin components of one long-running Seattle broadcast plaza.

reading.body:
KOMO Plaza West is a shared address in Lower Queen Anne, Seattle, assigned to one of two adjacent buildings within a multi-use complex that houses Sinclair Broadcast Group's television studios. The facility publishes no power specification, IT load, cooling capacity, or accelerator inventory. Without these figures, whether this site hosts meaningful AI compute capacity cannot be determined from available data.

Washington State has published power specifications for only two data center facilities totaling 60 MW across 46 mapped locations. KOMO Plaza West ranks third by published megawatts in the state, a ranking that reflects the absence of a published specification rather than a measured capacity, since the two facilities that do publish specifications account for all documented capacity in the state.

This campus matters to AI infrastructure assessment only if Sinclair Broadcast Group chooses to publish the power and cooling specifications of its Seattle facility. Until those facts appear in operator disclosures, KOMO Plaza West remains a mapped location without a measured role in the grid constraints that bind AI scaling.
